name: SimpleHC
tagline: Four residual streams with identity transitions, full-state read/write gates, and gate inputs shared over four sublayers.
description: SimpleHC on the full-attention shell: the embedding is replicated into four 1536-wide streams, each sublayer reads a weighted sum of the streams and adds its weighted output back without stream-to-stream mixing (identity transitions), and consecutive groups of four sublayers generate their sigmoid read and 2·sigmoid write gates from one normalized group-entry state. Within each group, earlier sublayer outputs reach later sublayer inputs through exact scalar dot-product corrections d_{j,k} = h_pre_j · h_post_k, writing back to the four streams once at the group boundary. Keeps Dense's 23 layers and FFN 6144 at +0.441% of the shared budget.
paperTitle: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability
mechanism: Four 1536-wide streams with identity residual transitions: no learned stream-mixing matrix or Sinkhorn projection
Groups of 4 sublayers (11×4 + 2 over 46 sublayers) share one normalized 6144-wide gate input; read = σ, write = 2σ
Intra-group scalar corrections d_{j,k} = h_pre_j · h_post_k propagate outputs without materializing intermediate 4×1536 states
limitations: Single seed 42. Read results as paired differences from Standard Residual (both use 23 full-attention layers and FFN 6144; mHC narrows FFN to 6016). Expresses the paper's shared-memory-access algebra in PyTorch without its fused DeepGEMM/Triton kernels; gate parameters train in the shared auxiliary AdamW group without weight decay. Parameters, memory and speed are outcomes, not controls.
